S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).

subtypes.Anhedonia for Happiness: Unable to feel happiness or joy even when good things happen.
subtypes.Lack of Satisfaction: Unable to experience satisfaction or pride even after achieving something good.
subtypes.Inability to Feel Love: Feeling numb to love or affection towards family or lovers.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where the mind feels empty and nothing is felt, as if all positive emotions are blocked.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops following exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, either directly, as a witness, or through repeated exposure to aversive details. It is characterized by persistent re-experiencing of the trauma, avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and marked changes in arousal and reactivity lasting more than one month with associated functional impairment. The clinical course can be acute or chronic, with symptoms sometimes emerging after a delayed interval or becoming exacerbated by new stressors or reminders. PTSD is distinguished from other anxiety and mood disorders by the clear temporal and phenomenological link to a qualifying traumatic event and the prominence of trauma-specific re-experiencing and avoidance phenomena.

patient.stressor: Roughly a year and a few months ago, Maria flew back to Guatemala after her younger cousin, whom she had helped mentor from afar, was killed during an armed robbery on a bus. She arrived in time to help with funeral arrangements and was present when the family viewed the body and recounted the circumstances of the attack in graphic detail, with local news replaying footage of the crime scene. Returning to New York, she tried to regain her structured routine of Agile projects, salsa nights, and hikes along the Hudson, but she found that anything related to buses, crowded public transit, or news about violence in Latin America became overwhelming, and she began to pull back from community events that might bring up conversations about the incident. After her manager noted a drop in her usual engagement at work and her husband pointed out how much she was avoiding trips back to Guatemala and even planning them, she brought up her ongoing distress with her primary care provider, who referred her to psychiatry when it was clear the trauma around her cousin’s death was still affecting her life and relationships.
patient.chief_complaint: “I go out of my way to avoid anything that reminds me of what happened to my cousin, even if it means cutting out parts of my life.”

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to live for salsa nights and weekend hikes, but now even when I force myself to go I just feel flat and disconnected, like I’m watching someone else’s life and would rather just be home on the couch scrolling mindlessly.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie in bed exhausted but wired, dozing off for an hour or two and then jolting awake from these vivid dreams about buses or my family back home, and after that I just toss and turn until my alarm goes off and I feel like I never really slept.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Out of nowhere—at my desk, on the subway, even cooking dinner—I’ll suddenly see my cousin’s body in the coffin or hear my aunt describing the shooting, like a horrible clip playing in my head that I can’t pause, and my chest tightens and I just freeze for a minute.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I avoid anything that might bring it up—no buses, no Spanish news, I’ve stopped going to Guatemalan community events and even muted family group chats—because I’m terrified that if I hear one more story or see one more image I’ll completely fall apart.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I remember the airport, the wake, and the burial in sharp detail, but there are big blank spots around when we viewed his body and some of the conversations about what happened on the bus, like whole chunks of that day are just missing when I try to piece it together.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).
S074.manifestation: Underneath everything I do, there’s this constant mix of dread and guilt, like I failed him by not being there or not getting him out of Guatemala sooner, and it colors even ordinary days so they all feel heavy and slightly wrong.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).
S076.manifestation: Even when something objectively good happens—like my team shipping a big release or my daughter getting an award at school—I smile and say the right things, but inside it feels muted and distant, like I’m going through the motions and can’t actually feel happy or close to anyone.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.
S078.manifestation: Since all this happened I’ve caught myself driving way too fast on the highway, drinking more than I should on weeknights, and taking on impossible workloads at the office, almost like I don’t care what happens to me as long as I don’t have to sit still with my thoughts.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.
S080.manifestation: If someone walks up behind me at work or a car backfires on the street, I jump out of my skin—my heart races, my whole body tenses, and even after I realize it’s nothing, it takes a long time for me to calm back down.
